findings.title: Reaching a bound through its focused step button disables that same control

evidence.excerpt: for (const button of buttons) button.disabled = Number(button.dataset.sliderStep) < 0 ? value <= min : value >= max;

findings.impact: A keyboard user can activate a step button to reach an endpoint; validate immediately makes the focused button disabled. This can lose the visible focus/continuation point. Existing endpoint checks operate the range instead, so they do not exercise this interaction.
findings.proposal: Preserve a deliberate focus target before disabling the focused step, or keep an aria-disabled step focusable with an explicit no-op bound guard. Keep existing native disabling when appropriate for controls that are not focused.
acceptance: Focus the increase button with draft one step below maximum, activate using Enter or Space and verify the draft reaches the exact endpoint and focus remains on a visible meaningful control.
Repeat at the minimum with decrease; continue editing without needing to restart the tab sequence.
Confirm endpoint guards, invalid-input recovery, disabled no-JavaScript behaviour and reported-value separation still hold.

resolution.summary: The exact-value field receives focus before the active endpoint step button is disabled. A focused Enter-to-maximum and Space-to-minimum regression was added. This review verified source only; execution remains pending.

evidence.excerpt: test('a keyboard step to either endpoint preserves focus on the exact-value field'
